title: Torus torsion quotients jointly detect Laurent polynomials over any ring
statement: Let $B$ be any commutative ring, $r\geq0$ an integer, and let $L_B=B[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$ denote the ring of finite formal sums $\sum_{u\in\mathbf Z^r}b_ut^u$ with coefficientwise addition and multiplication determined by $t^ut^v=t^{u+v}$. For $n\geq1$, put $J_n=(t_1^n-1,\ldots,t_r^n-1)\subset L_B$ and let $q_n:L_B\to L_B/J_n$ be the quotient homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Then $\bigcap_{n\geq1}J_n=0$. Equivalently, for $f,g\in L_B$, if $q_n(f)=q_n(g)$ for every integer $n\geq1$, then $f=g$. When $r=0$, the ring $L_B$ is $B$ and every $J_n$ is zero.

source.place: Theorem 12.33, printed p.243, and Theorem 12.36, proof on printed pp.243--244: joint injectivity after tensoring with the parameter algebra; split-torus case over arbitrary coefficients.

proof.text: If $r=0$, there is one exponent vector, so $L_B=B$. The ideal generated by the empty list is zero, giving the asserted intersection. Hence assume $r>0$ for the intersection calculation; the final quotient-kernel step also applies when $r=0$.

source.place: Theorem 12.33, printed p.243, and Theorem 12.36, printed pp.243--244; agent expansion of the split-torus coefficient argument over arbitrary B

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ and $a\in(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r$, define $S_{n,a}(h)=\sum_{u\bmod n=a}h_u$, where $h=\sum_u h_ut^u$ and only its finite support is summed. These are $B$-linear functions: for addition sum over the union of the two finite supports, padding with zero coefficients, and distribute the finite sum; scalar multiplication is coefficientwise.

source.place: Theorem 12.33, printed p.243, and Theorem 12.36, printed pp.243--244; agent expansion of the split-torus coefficient argument over arbitrary B

proof.text: Let $e_i$ be the $i$th coordinate vector. Multiplication by $t_i^n$ sends the coefficient $h_u$ to exponent $u+ne_i$. Translation is a bijection on the finite support and preserves its residue classes, so $S_{n,a}(ht_i^n)=S_{n,a}(h)$. Thus $S_{n,a}(h(t_i^n-1))=0$. Every element of the generated ideal $J_n$ has the form $\sum_{i=1}^rh_i(t_i^n-1)$, by distributing finite sums of multiples of its generators. Linearity therefore gives $S_{n,a}(J_n)=0$ for every $a$.

source.place: Theorem 12.33, printed p.243, and Theorem 12.36, printed pp.243--244; agent expansion of the split-torus coefficient argument over arbitrary B

proof.text: Let $f\in\bigcap_{n\geq1}J_n$, with finite support $F$. If $F$ is empty, $f=0$. Otherwise take $M=\max(\{0\}\cup\{|u_i|:u\in F,1\leq i\leq r\})$ and $n=2M+1$. If $u,v\in F$ have the same residue vector modulo $n$, each $u_i-v_i$ is divisible by $n$ and has absolute value at most $2M<n$, so it is zero. Hence $u=v$. For each $u\in F$ this gives $f_u=S_{n,u\bmod n}(f)=0$ by the preceding step, since $f\in J_n$. All coefficients vanish, so $f=0$ as a formal sum. Conversely zero lies in every ideal.

source.place: Theorem 12.33, printed p.243, and Theorem 12.36, printed pp.243--244; agent expansion of the split-torus coefficient argument over arbitrary B

proof.text: The quotient homomorphism has kernel $J_n$ by [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Thus $q_n(f)=q_n(g)$ for all $n$ is equivalent to $f-g\in\bigcap_nJ_n$, and the intersection calculation gives $f=g$. Conversely joint injectivity applied to $f$ and $0$ proves the intersection assertion.

Source: Milne AG 2017 Thm 12.33 and 12.36 proof, printed pp.243-244 (PDF pp.255-256). The item writes out the injectivity Milne calls obvious, directly over an arbitrary ring B, and avoids his step that tensoring preserves joint injectivity. Step checks: (1) r=0 gives J_n=0. (2) The residue sums S_{n,a} are B-linear. (3) Translating by n e_i preserves residues, so S kills each generator multiple and, by linearity, all of J_n. (4) With n=2M+1, distinct support points have distinct residues, so f_u=S_{n,u mod n}(f)=0. (5) The cited def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient statement says the quotient map has kernel J (checked); its hypotheses hold with D=L_B, R=B, J=J_n; the converse follows with g=0. proof_deps equals the union of uses; marking steps elementary is justified. Edge cases tested: B=0, r=0, 2(t^{-1}-t) over Z/4 (killed at n=2, detected at n=3), F_p with p dividing n, nilpotent coefficients. Duplicate search (rg -L laurent over the DAG) found only the univariate field node and the parent. The parent lem-sfb-connected-action-torus-rigidity step 3 uses arbitrary B and rank d, which the item covers. Route: only a definition is cited; no tool_uses; no SGA. The Mathlib search record is adequate.

lean.statement: theorem torus_torsion_joint_injectivity (B : Type u) [CommRing B] (r : ℕ) : (⨅ (n : ℕ) (_ : 0 < n), torusTorsionIdeal B r n) = ⊥ ∧ (∀ f g : AddMonoidAlgebra B (Fin r → ℤ), (∀ (n : ℕ) (_ : 0 < n), Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ B (torusTorsionIdeal B r n) f = Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ B (torusTorsionIdeal B r n) g) → f = g) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (_ : 0 < n), torusTorsionIdeal B 0 n = ⊥)
